niche: each municipality's vacancy share in a heated Norwegian November estimated from the electricity hub's hourly meter loads, with the population register's overcoverage, undercoverage and net bias measured against it, certified for a 2027 grant
answer: Five municipalities qualify: Tverrvika, Hesteby, Solmoen, Ørnevik and Fjordeid (396 of 8,020 counted dwellings vacant); the register's overcoverage 118 (1.6 per cent), undercoverage 556 (66.7 per cent), net bias 5.5 per cent
answer_source: task5/submission.md, Final Recommendation and Supplementary Questions
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the cadastre and the meter reads correctly and reads the regulation rejects the consumption floor (empty dwellings are heated in November, so the vacant use more than the lived-in), reads occupancy from the household's morning or evening rise over the dwelling's night-time use on any day, sees it separate bimodally and agree with the register, and files that Tverrvika and Ørnevik alone qualify; 70 vacant dwellings heated on a daily timer rise every day and read as lived in.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each municipality's vacancy share, an official estimate of true occupancy built from two error-prone administrative sources, the population register and each dwelling's own hourly load, read for what a household does that the building's own heating, on a timer or not, does not repeat; with wards for dwellings there is no heating left on an empty home's timer, no register that lags and no household's day.

world.geography: Norway (a fictional county of ten municipalities)

driver: The decisive quantity is whether each unit was in use during a window, seen only through a continuous meter whose level and daily shape are both carried by a load that runs on a schedule whether or not anyone uses the unit, so use is a day departing from what the unit's own record repeats, beyond its scheduled load and noise.
driver_concrete: A dwelling counts as vacant when nobody lived in it in the reference fortnight, whatever the population register shows; an empty Norwegian dwelling is heated through November, and one left on its heaters' daily timer also rises every morning and evening at its comfort hours, so neither the level nor the daily rise shows a household; only a day departing from the dwelling's own typical day does.
stump: A competent solver conforms the cadastre and the hub's hourly values, sees that an empty dwelling in a Norwegian November is heated so no consumption floor works, reads occupancy from the household's morning or evening rise over the dwelling's own night-time use, sees it separate cleanly and agree with the register, and files that Tverrvika and Ørnevik alone qualify (6.2 and 7.1 per cent); 70 vacant dwellings were left heated on a daily timer that rises at the same hours by the same amount every day, and only a household's departure from what the dwelling repeats every day, some hour more than 0.9 kWh above its own typical day, shows that someone lived there, which designates five.

lineage.driver: Activity at each site is seen through a sensor that records every event of some units and none of others, and the units it never records are spread unevenly across sites, so the missing activity is not a fixed share of what the sensor saw: it is rebuilt as the never-recorded units based at each site times the activity per such unit that the fully counted sites show, while one seen-to-counted ratio moves the missing activity from the sites holding those units to the sites whose units are all recorded.
